subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Piezoelectric Materials: Electricity From Pressure
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Piezoelectric Materials: Electricity From Pressure.

hook.text: Step on a piezoelectric tile and it generates electricity. Millions of footsteps in a train station could power its lighting.

buildup.text: Piezoelectric crystals produce voltage when squeezed. The lattice deforms, displacing charges and creating an electric potential.

discovery.text: Tokyo's train stations tested piezoelectric floors. Each step generates about 10 milliwatts. Scale makes it viable.

twist.text: The energy per step is minuscule. Harvesting it costs more than generating it from solar panels. The economics don't work — yet.

climax.text: Piezoelectrics already power quartz watches, ultrasound machines, and fuel injectors. Energy harvesting is the newest frontier.

punchline.text: Squeeze a crystal. Get voltage. Every step is a tiny power plant.

quiz.question: Why hasn't piezoelectric energy harvesting from foot traffic become widespread?
options: The vibrations from footsteps are too irregular for consistent power generation
Each step generates only about 10 milliwatts, making it more expensive than solar
Piezoelectric materials wear out after a few thousand compressions
